work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 小學書題 소학서제 · Zhu Xi's Title Preface (1187) · 小學書題 1 … 小學書題 6

items.text: Love your father and mother.
items.quote: 어버이ᄅᆞᆯ ᄉᆞ랑ᄒᆞ며 — Love parents.

items.text: Honor your elders.
items.quote: 얼운을 고ᇰ겨ᇰᄒᆞ며 — Honor elders.

items.text: While they are still young, have them study and practice these duties, so they grow with wisdom and become habit.
items.quote: 반ᄃᆞ시 ᄒᆡ여곰 그 졈어 어려실제 가ᇰᄒᆞ야 니기게 홈은 — Must have them learn and practice while young.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 立敎第一 립교 뎨일 · Establishing the Teaching · 立敎 9 … 立敎 13

items.text: Be gentle, harmonious, and filial in manner; do not be arrogant or rely on your own strength.
items.quote: 溫柔孝弟，毋驕恃力 — Be gentle, filial, and respectful; do not be proud or trust in force.

items.text: Practice fraternal respect; be obedient and harmonious toward your elder siblings.
items.quote: 溫柔孝弟，毋驕恃力 — Be gentle, filial, and respectful; do not be proud or trust in force.

items.text: At home, be filial to your parents.
items.quote: 弟子入則孝 — A young person, at home, should be filial.

items.text: Outside the home, show respectful deference to your elder siblings and elders.
items.quote: 出則弟 — Away from home, be respectful to elders.

items.text: Serve your parents with all your strength, holding nothing back.
items.quote: 事父母，能竭其力 — Serve parents, exerting all your strength.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 敬身第三 경신 · Reverencing the Person · 明心術之要 (the essentials of the mind) · 敬身 1 … 敬身 11

items.text: Reverence your own body as your parents' branch; do not harm your parents by harming yourself.
items.quote: 身也者，親之枝也。敢不敬與。不能敬其身，是傷其親。

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 明倫第二 며ᇰ륜 뎨이라 · Clarifying Human Relations · 明父子之親 (parent and child) · 明倫 1 … 明倫 4

items.text: Rise at cockcrow, wash, rinse your mouth, comb your hair, and dress properly before going to serve your parents.
items.quote: 子事父母, 鷄初鳴, 咸盥漱, 櫛縰笄總 — A child serving parents: at cockcrow, all wash, rinse, comb, bind the hair.

items.text: Serve your parents-in-law as your own parents: rise at cockcrow, wash, rinse your mouth, comb your hair, and dress properly.
items.quote: 婦事舅姑如事父母, 鷄初鳴, 咸盥漱, 櫛縰笄總 — A daughter-in-law serves parents-in-law as parents; at cockcrow, all wash, rinse, comb, bind.

items.text: Enter your parents' presence with lowered voice and pleasant manner, ask about their warmth and comfort, and respectfully attend to any pain or itch.
items.quote: 下氣怡聲, 問衣燠寒, 疾痛苛癢, 而敬抑搔之 — Lower the voice, ask about clothes' warmth, and respectfully press or scratch where it hurts or itches.

items.text: When your parents go out or come in, walk before or behind them and reverently support them.
items.quote: 出入則或先或後, 而敬扶持之 — Going out or coming in, go before or behind, and respectfully support them.

items.text: When offering water for washing, the younger holds the basin, the elder pours the water, and after washing hand them the towel.
items.quote: 進盥, 少者奉槃, 長者奉水, 請沃盥, 盥卒授巾 — Presenting wash water: the young hold the basin, the elder pour the water; after washing, give the towel.

items.text: Ask what your parents wish to eat or drink, respectfully offer it, and do not withdraw until they have tasted it.
items.quote: 問所欲而敬進之, 柔色以溫之, 父母舅姑, 必嘗之而後退 — Ask what they desire, respectfully present it; parents and parents-in-law must taste it before you withdraw.

items.text: At dawn go to your parents, ask what they will eat or drink; if they have not eaten, help the elders prepare the meal.
items.quote: 昧爽而朝, 問何食飮矣. 若己食則退, 若未食則佐長者視具 — At dawn, go in and ask what they will eat; if already eaten, withdraw; if not, help the elders see to the meal.

items.text: All in the household, inner and outer, rise at cockcrow, wash, dress, put away bedding, sweep the rooms and court, spread mats, and each attend to your tasks.
items.quote: 凡內外鷄初鳴, 咸盥漱, 衣服. 斂枕簟, 灑掃室堂及庭, 布席. 各從其事 — All within and without: at cockcrow, wash, dress, put away pillows and mats, sweep, spread mats, each attend to their work.

items.text: When your parents are about to sit or lie down, present the mat and ask which way they want it; the younger hold the bed and seat, and arrange the bedding.
items.quote: 父母舅姑, 將坐, 奉席請何鄕. 將衽, 長者奉席請何趾, 少者執牀與坐 — When parents or parents-in-law are to sit, present a mat and ask which way; when to lie down, the elder presents the mat, the young hold the bed.

items.text: Do not move or use your parents' clothes, bedding, mats, pillows, or armrests; respect their staff and shoes, and do not eat or drink from their vessels unless it is their leftover.
items.quote: 父母舅姑之衣衾簟席枕几不傳. 杖屨, 祗敬之, 勿敢近. 敦牟巵匜, 非餕, 莫敢用 — Do not move parents' clothes, bedding, mats, pillows, armrest; revere their staff and shoes; do not use their vessels except for leftovers.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 明倫第二 며ᇰ륜 뎨이라 · Clarifying Human Relations · 明君臣之義 (ruler and subject) · 明倫 53 … 明倫 明君臣之義 右

items.text: Do not deceive your ruler; rather, oppose him when he is wrong.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, 明倫 明君臣之義
items.quote: 勿欺也. 而犯之. — Do not deceive; rather, oppose.

items.text: Do not be a petty man anxious about gain or loss; serve your ruler with a single heart.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, 明倫 明君臣之義
items.quote: 其未得之也, 患得之. 旣得之, 患失之. — Before gaining, he worries about gaining; after gaining, he worries about losing.

items.text: Reprove your ruler with hard demands, set good before him and block evil, and never say he is incapable.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, 明倫 明君臣之義
items.quote: 責難於君, 謂之恭. 陳善閉邪, 謂之敬. 吾君不能, 謂之賊. — Demanding difficult things of the ruler is respect; presenting good and blocking evil is reverence; saying my ruler cannot is being a thief.

items.text: If you hold office and cannot fulfill its duties, or if your counsel is ignored, resign.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, 明倫 明君臣之義
items.quote: 有官守者, 不得其職則去. 有言責者, 不得其言則去. — One with office, if he cannot fulfill duties, leaves; one with duty to speak, if words not heeded, leaves.

items.text: Serve one ruler only; do not transfer your loyalty to another.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, 明倫 明君臣之義
items.quote: 忠臣不事二君 — A loyal minister does not serve two rulers.

items.text: Be faithful to your husband alone; do not remarry.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, 明倫 明君臣之義
items.quote: 烈女不更二夫 — A chaste woman does not change to a second husband.
items.conflict: 1 Corinthians 7:39-40 allows a widow to remarry

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 明倫第二 며ᇰ륜 뎨이라 · Clarifying Human Relations · 通論 (general discussion) · 明倫 102 … 明倫 通論 右

items.text: Cultivate the goodwill of your relatives before seeking friends outside; do not neglect the near for the far.
items.quote: 親戚不說, 不敢外交 — If relatives are not pleased, do not dare to make outside friendships.

items.text: Serve your parents with filial piety while they are alive, for after their death it is too late.
items.quote: 親戚旣沒, 雖欲孝, 誰爲孝 — If relatives are dead, though you wish to be filial, for whom?

items.text: Honor your elder sibling now; do not delay until old age, when the opportunity is lost.
items.quote: 年旣耆艾, 雖欲悌, 誰爲悌 — When age is already old, though you wish to be respectful to elder brother, for whom?

items.text: Do not let your love for your wife and children weaken your devotion to your parents; hold fast to the end.
items.quote: 孝衰於妻子 — Filial piety declines because of wife and children.

items.text: As one younger, willingly serve your elders and do not refuse.
items.quote: 幼而不肯事長 — The young are unwilling to serve their elders.

items.text: Nurture your affection for your son day by day and never let it lapse.
items.quote: 父子之親, 則日切磋而不舍也 — The affection between father and son, daily polish and do not abandon.

items.text: Nurture your affection for your father day by day and never let it lapse.
items.quote: 父子之親, 則日切磋而不舍也 — The affection between father and son, daily polish and do not abandon.

items.text: Keep the proper distinction between husband and wife, and work at it daily without slackening.
items.quote: 夫婦之別, 則日切磋而不舍也 — The distinction between husband and wife, daily polish and do not abandon.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 小學題辭 소학제사 · Zhu Xi's Inscription · 小學題辭 1 … 小學題辭 11

items.text: Love your parents.
items.quote: 어버이ᄅᆞᆯ ᄉᆞ라ᇰᄒᆞ며 — Love your parents.

items.text: Respect your elder brother.
items.quote: 혀ᇰ을 고ᇰ겨ᇰ홈과 — Respect your elder brother.

items.text: Be deferential and obedient to your elders.
items.quote: 얼운의게 고ᇰ슌홈이 — Be deferential to elders.

items.text: Be filial at home and do not be disobedient in speech.
items.quote: 들어ᄂᆞᆫ 효도ᄒᆞ고 ... 닐뮈매 혹(或)도 거슬ᄧᅳ게 마롤디니 — At home be filial; do not be disobedient in speech.

items.text: When you have remaining strength, serve your parents.
items.quote: 행홈애 남ᄋᆞᆫ 히미 잇거든 모시외오며 — If you have remaining strength, serve them.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 明倫第二 며ᇰ륜 뎨이라 · Clarifying Human Relations · 明父子之親 (parent and child) · 明倫 35 … 明倫 明父子之親 右

items.text: Love and respect your parents above all; to love or respect others instead of them is contrary to virtue and propriety.
items.quote: 不愛其親, 而愛他人者, 謂之悖德. 不敬其親, 而敬他人者, 謂之悖禮. — Do not love others without loving your parents; do not honor others without honoring your parents.

items.text: In daily life at home, show your parents the utmost respect.
items.quote: 居則致其敬 — In daily life, show utmost respect.

items.text: When you support your parents, do it with joy, not merely as a duty.
items.quote: 養則致其樂 — In supporting them, show utmost joy.

items.text: When your parents are ill, be deeply anxious and troubled for them.
items.quote: 病則致其憂 — In illness, show utmost worry.

items.text: At your parents' funeral, grieve with deepest sorrow.
items.quote: 喪則致其哀 — In mourning, show utmost grief.

items.text: In ancestral rites for your parents, be solemn and reverent.
items.quote: 祭則致其嚴 — In sacrifice, show utmost solemnity.
items.conflict: Conflicts with the biblical teaching that the dead are not to be worshiped and that worship belongs to God alone (Exodus 20:3-5; Deuteronomy 18:10-12).

items.text: Do not be arrogant in high position, rebellious in low position, or contentious among equals, lest you bring ruin, punishment, or injury upon yourself and thus fail your parents.
items.quote: 居上不驕, 爲下不亂, 在醜不爭. 三者不除, 雖日用三牲之養, 猶爲不孝也. — If you do not avoid these three, even daily offerings of three animals are still unfilial.

items.text: Do not be lazy, addicted to gambling and drink, partial to your wife and children, indulgent in lust, or quarrelsome; these five behaviors neglect or endanger your parents and are unfilial.
items.quote: 惰其四支, 不顧父母之養; 博奕好飮酒; 好貨財私妻子; 從耳目之欲以爲父母戮; 好勇鬪狠以危父母. — The five unfilial things: laziness, gambling and drinking, loving wealth and favoring wife and children, following lusts, and fighting.

items.text: Treat your body as your parents' legacy: be serious at home, loyal to your ruler, reverent in office, trustworthy with friends, and courageous in battle, so that no disaster falls on your parents.
items.quote: 身也者, 父母之遺體也... 五者不遂, 灾及其親. — The body is your parents' legacy; if these five are not accomplished, disaster reaches your parents.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 立敎第一 립교 뎨일 · Establishing the Teaching · 立敎 1 … 立敎 3

items.text: While pregnant, keep your body and mind pure: avoid improper foods, sights, and sounds, so that the child may be born well-formed and talented.
items.quote: 目不視邪色, 耳不聽淫聲 — Eyes do not look at evil colors, ears do not listen to licentious sounds.

items.text: Choose for your infant a teacher who is generous, kind, gentle, respectful, careful, and sparing of words.
items.quote: 必求其寬裕慈惠溫良恭敬愼而寡言者, 使爲子師 — Seek one who is generous, kind, gentle, respectful, careful, and sparing of words; make him the child's teacher.

items.text: Instruct your child at each stage: teach right-hand eating and proper speech, at six numbers and directions, at seven separation of boys and girls, at eight deference to elders, at nine the calendar, and at ten send him to an outside teacher for writing, arithmetic, and deportment.
items.quote: 子能食食敎以右手. 六年敎之數與方名 — When he can eat, teach him to use his right hand. At six, teach numbers and directions.

items.text: Do not let her go out at ten; have her learn obedience, work with hemp and silk, and weave clothing for the household.
items.quote: 執麻枲, 治絲繭. 織紝組紃, 學女事, 以共衣服 — Work hemp and silk, weave and braid, learn women's work to provide clothing.

items.text: Teach her to observe the sacrifices, present the wine and dishes, and assist in the offerings according to rite.
items.quote: 觀於祭祀, 納酒漿籩豆葅醢, 禮相助奠 — Observe at sacrifices; present wine, baskets, and dishes; assist the offerings according to rite.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship is idolatry; honor parents but offer no sacrifices to the dead (Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: Give her in marriage at twenty (or twenty-three if there is cause) by proper betrothal, not by elopement.
items.quote: 十有五年而笄, 二十而嫁. 有故二十三而嫁 — At fifteen she is pinned; at twenty she marries; if there is cause, at twenty-three.

items.text: Practice filial piety earnestly toward your parents.
items.quote: 惇行孝悌 — Earnestly practice filial piety and fraternal respect.

items.text: Show brotherly respect and obedience to your elder brother.
items.quote: 惇行孝悌 — Earnestly practice filial piety and fraternal respect.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 明倫第二 며ᇰ륜 뎨이라 · Clarifying Human Relations · 明朋友之交 (friends) · 明倫 86 … 明倫 明朋友之交 右

items.text: Meet with friends through culture, and use friendship to help one another in benevolence.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part, Clarifying Human Relations, 明朋友之交
items.quote: 君子以文會友, 以友輔仁 — The superior man uses culture to meet friends, and uses friends to support benevolence.

items.text: Be earnest and sincere with friends.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part, Clarifying Human Relations, 明朋友之交
items.quote: 朋友切切偲偲 — Friends should be earnest and urgant.

items.text: Be harmonious and joyful with your brothers and sisters.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part, Clarifying Human Relations, 明朋友之交
items.quote: 兄弟怡怡 — brothers should be harmonious.

items.text: Reprove a friend for his good; this is the way of friendship.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part, Clarifying Human Relations, 明朋友之交
items.quote: 責善, 朋友道也 — Reproving for good is the way of friends.

items.text: Give faithful counsel and guide your friend well; if it is not accepted, stop, and do not bring shame on yourself.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part, Clarifying Human Relations, 明朋友之交
items.quote: 忠告而善道之, 不可則止, 毋自辱焉 — Faithfully advise and skillfully guide; if not possible, stop, do not bring disgrace on yourself.

items.text: Befriend the benevolent among the scholars when dwelling in a state.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part, Clarifying Human Relations, 明朋友之交
items.quote: 友其士之仁者 — befriend its benevolent scholars.

items.text: Choose friends who are upright, sincere, and well-informed; avoid those who are flattering, ingratiating, or smooth-tongued.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part, Clarifying Human Relations, 明朋友之交
items.quote: 友直, 友諒, 友多聞, 益矣. 友便辟, 友善柔, 友便佞, 損矣 — Friends who are upright, sincere, and learned are helpful; friends who are obsequious, flattering, and glib are harmful.

items.text: Do not presume on age, rank, or family connections in friendship; befriend for virtue alone.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part, Clarifying Human Relations, 明朋友之交
items.quote: 不挾長, 不挾貴, 不挾兄弟而友. 友也者, 友其德也. 不可以有挾也 — Do not rely on seniority, wealth, or powerful relatives to make friends. Friendship is for virtue; one cannot have such reliance.

items.text: Do not exhaust a friend's good will or loyalty; so preserve the friendship.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part, Clarifying Human Relations, 明朋友之交
items.quote: 君子不盡人之歡, 不竭人之忠, 以全交也 — The superior man does not exhaust others' goodwill or loyalty, to preserve the friendship.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 明倫第二 며ᇰ륜 뎨이라 · Clarifying Human Relations · 明長幼之序 (elder and younger) · 明倫 83 … 明倫 明長幼之序 右

items.text: Do not ask a senior much above you his age; when you meet him informally, do not convey messages; when you meet him on the road, if he sees you, come forward, but do not ask where he is going.
items.quote: 尊長於己踰等，不敢問其年。燕見不將命，遇於道見則面，不請所之 — Do not ask a senior above you his age; on an informal visit do not carry a message; on meeting him in the road, show yourself if he sees you, and do not ask where he is going.

items.text: When sitting with a senior, if he does not bid you, do not take up a lute, draw on the ground, move your hands, or fan; if he is lying down, kneel to carry his message.
items.quote: 侍坐弗使，不執琴瑟，不畵地，手無容，不翣也，寢則坐而將命 — When sitting with a senior, unless he bids you, do not play the qin, draw, gesture, or fan; if he lies down, kneel to carry his message.

items.text: When attending your elder in archery, gather the arrows; in pitch-pot, hold the arrows; if you win, wash the cup and present it to him.
items.quote: 侍射則約矢，侍投則擁矢，勝則洗而以請 — When attending archery, gather the arrows; when attending pitch-pot, hold the arrows; if you win, wash the cup and present it.

items.text: Walk behind a man of your father's age; walk a little behind a man of your elder brother's age in echelon.
items.quote: 父之齒隨行，兄之齒鴈行 — Walk behind a man of your father's age, and in echelon with one of your elder brother's age.

items.text: Do not overtake a friend when walking together.
items.quote: 朋友不相踰 — Friends do not overtake one another.

items.text: When carrying burdens together, combine light loads and divide heavy ones, so that a gray-haired person does not carry anything.
items.quote: 輕任幷，重任分，頒白者不提挈 — Combine light burdens, divide heavy burdens, so that the gray-haired do not carry.

items.text: Do not let an aged man of rank walk on foot; do not let an aged commoner eat a meal without meat.
items.quote: 君子耆老，不徒行，庶人耆老不徒食 — An aged man of rank does not walk on foot; an aged commoner does not eat plain rice.

items.text: When you drink with villagers, do not leave until the old men with staffs have left.
items.quote: 鄕人飮酒，杖者出，斯出矣 — When villagers drink, when the staff-bearers go out, then go out.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 立敎第一 립교 뎨일 · Establishing the Teaching · 立敎 4 … 立敎 8

items.text: Show your young child that you do not deceive; train him to stand straight and listen attentively.
items.quote: 幼子常視毋誑, 立必正方, 不傾聽 — Show a young child no deceit; have him stand straight and not listen carelessly.

items.text: Love your son and maintain close affection between you.
items.quote: 父子有親 — Father and son have affection.

items.text: Love your father and maintain close affection between you.
items.quote: 父子有親 — Father and son have affection.

items.text: Maintain the proper distinction between husband and wife in conduct and roles.
items.quote: 夫婦有別 — Husband and wife have distinction.

items.text: Honor your elders and yield to them, keeping proper order between older and younger.
items.quote: 長幼有序 — Elder and younger have order.

items.text: Practice filial piety toward your parents.
items.quote: 孝 — filial piety.

items.text: Love your brothers and sisters with brotherly love; be friendly to them.
items.quote: 友 — brotherly love.

items.text: Be harmonious with your paternal relatives and close to your maternal relatives.
items.quote: 睦婣 — harmony with paternal kin, closeness with maternal kin.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 敬身第三 경신 · Reverencing the Person · 明威儀之則 (rules of deportment) · 敬身 24 … 敬身 明威儀之則 右

items.text: Be filial to your father.
items.quote: 言孝悌于父兄 — speak about being filial and respectful to father and elder brothers.

items.text: Be respectful to your elder brother.
items.quote: 言孝悌于父兄 — speak about being filial and respectful to father and elder brothers.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 明倫第二 며ᇰ륜 뎨이라 · Clarifying Human Relations · 明父子之親 (parent and child) · 明倫 29 … 明倫 34

items.text: When offering the ancestral sacrifice, husband and wife together must personally perform it, each fulfilling the inner and outer offices.
items.quote: 夫祭也者, 必夫婦親之 — In sacrifice, husband and wife must personally conduct it.
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead are forbidden (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: Preside over the ancestral sacrifice in person; only with a valid reason may you send another in your place.
items.quote: 君子之祭也, 必身親莅之. 有故則使人可也 — A noble man's sacrifice, he must personally preside; if there is a reason, he may send another.
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead are forbidden (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: During the purification days, fix your thoughts on the departed: their dwelling, words, intentions, joys, and tastes, so that after three days you may behold them.
items.quote: 齊之日, 思其居處, 思其笑語, 思其志意, 思其所樂, 思其所嗜 — During the purification days, think of their dwelling, laughter, speech, intentions, joys, tastes.
items.conflict: Communion with the dead conflicts with Deut 18:10-12.

items.text: On the day of sacrifice, enter the shrine with awe, as if seeing the departed in their place, hearing their voice and sighs.
items.quote: 祭之日, 入室僾然必有見乎其位... 必有聞乎其嘆息之聲 — On the day of sacrifice, entering the shrine, you must see them in their place... hear their sighs.
items.conflict: Communion with the dead conflicts with Deut 18:10-12.

items.text: Keep the memory of departed parents vivid: their face before your eyes, their voice in your ears, their wishes in your heart; love and sincerity make them present, so reverence them.
items.quote: 色不忘乎目, 聲不絶乎耳, 心志嗜欲不忘乎心 — Their countenance never left their eyes, their voice never ceased in their ears, their intentions never forgotten.
items.conflict: Veneration of the dead conflicts with Deut 18:10-12.

items.text: Even in poverty, do not sell the sacrificial vessels; even in cold, do not wear the sacrificial garments; when building, do not cut the trees on the grave mound.
items.quote: 君子雖貧, 不粥祭器, 雖寒, 不衣祭服, 爲宮室, 不斬於丘木 — A noble man, though poor, does not sell sacrificial vessels; though cold, does not wear sacrificial garments; when building, does not cut trees on the grave mound.
items.conflict: Preserving vessels for ancestor rites conflicts with Deut 18:10-12.

items.text: Do not lend the sacrificial vessels; make the sacrificial vessels before making vessels for everyday use.
items.quote: 大夫祭器不假. 祭器未成, 不造燕器 — A great officer does not lend his sacrificial vessels; until the sacrificial vessels are complete, he does not make ordinary vessels.
items.conflict: Preserving vessels for ancestor rites conflicts with Deut 18:10-12.

items.text: Do not injure or harm your body, hair, or skin, for they were received from your parents; guard them as the beginning of filial piety.
items.quote: 身體髮膚, 受之父母. 不敢毁傷, 孝之始也 — The body, hair, and skin are received from parents; do not dare to injure or harm them—this is the beginning of filial piety.

items.text: Establish yourself in virtuous conduct and make your name known in later generations, so that you bring honor to your parents.
items.quote: 立身行道, 揚名於後世, 以顯父母, 孝之終也 — Establish yourself, practice the Way, make your name known in later generations to glorify parents.

items.text: Follow the way of heaven and the benefits of the earth; be careful in conduct and frugal in spending, so as to nourish your parents.
items.quote: 用天之道, 因地之利, 謹身節用, 以養父母 — Following the way of heaven, utilizing the benefits of the earth, being careful and frugal, to nourish parents.

items.text: Wear only the clothes, speak only the words, and do only the deeds that accord with the former kings' laws, so that you may preserve the ancestral temple.
items.quote: 非先王之法服, 不敢服... 然後能保其宗廟 — Not wearing clothing not prescribed... then can preserve ancestral temple.
items.conflict: Preserving ancestral temple conflicts with Deut 18:10-12.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 稽古第四 계고 · Examining the Ancients · 立敎 (establishing the teaching) · 稽古 1 … 稽古 立敎 右

items.text: While pregnant, keep your eyes from evil sights, your ears from lewd sounds, and your mouth from arrogant words, so that you teach your child in the womb.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, Examining the Ancients, Establishing the Teaching
items.quote: 目不視惡色, 耳不聽淫聲, 口不出敖言 — Eyes not see evil, ears not hear lewd, mouth not speak arrogant.

items.text: After the child is born, teach him so that from one thing he understands a hundred.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, Examining the Ancients, Establishing the Teaching
items.quote: 太任敎之以一而識百 — She taught him one thing and he knew a hundred.

items.text: Choose a dwelling place where your child will not learn bad ways; move away from a graveyard or marketplace and settle near a school.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, Examining the Ancients, Establishing the Teaching
items.quote: 此非所以居子也. 乃徙舍學宮之旁 — Not a place to raise a son; she moved near the school.

items.text: Do not deceive your child; if you promise something, carry it out, even at cost to yourself.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, Examining the Ancients, Establishing the Teaching
items.quote: 適有知而欺之, 是敎之不信. 乃買猪肉以食之 — Deceiving him now teaches distrust; bought pork and fed.

items.text: Command your son to study the Poetry (Shijing), for without it he will not be able to speak properly.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, Examining the Ancients, Establishing the Teaching
items.quote: 不學詩無以言 — Not learning Poetry, nothing to speak with.

items.text: Command your son to study the Rites (Liji), for without them he will not be able to take his stand.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, Examining the Ancients, Establishing the Teaching
items.quote: 不學禮無以立 — Not learning Rites, nothing to stand on.

items.text: Tell your son to study the Zhou Nan and Shao Nan chapters of the Poetry, for without them a man is like one standing with his face to a wall.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, Examining the Ancients, Establishing the Teaching
items.quote: 人而不爲周南召南, 其猶正墻面而立與也 — A man not studying Zhou Nan and Shao Nan is like facing a wall.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 明倫第二 며ᇰ륜 뎨이라 · Clarifying Human Relations · 通論 (general discussion) · 明倫 97 … 明倫 101

items.text: Serve your parents filially; when they are wrong, remonstrate gently rather than openly offending, and attend them constantly and work for them until death.
items.quote: 事親，有隱而無犯，左右就養，無方，服勤至死 — Serve parents: gentle remonstrance, constant attendance, labor to death.

items.text: Observe the full three-year mourning for a parent.
items.quote: 致喪三年 — Complete the mourning of three years.

items.text: Serve your father as one of the three to whom you owe your life, even unto death.
items.quote: 父生之；唯其所在，則致死焉 — Father gives life; where he is, go even to death.

items.text: When your father is unrighteous, remonstrate with him; do not keep silent.
items.quote: 故當不義，則子不可以弗爭於父 — When there is unrighteousness, a son must not fail to remonstrate with his father.

items.text: Serve your elder brother with respect and compliance.
items.quote: 弟敬而順 — Younger brother respects and obeys.

items.text: Love your younger brothers and treat them as friends.
items.quote: 兄愛而友 — Elder brother loves and is friendly.

items.text: Be kind to your children and teach them.
items.quote: 父慈而敎 — Father is kind and teaches.

items.text: Be gentle and upright with your wife.
items.quote: 夫和而義 — Husband is harmonious and righteous.

items.text: Be gentle and upright toward your husband.
items.quote: 妻柔而正 — Wife is gentle and upright.

items.text: Be kind to your daughter-in-law.
items.quote: 姑慈而從 — Mother-in-law is kind and compliant.

items.text: Obey your mother-in-law and be gentle.
items.quote: 婦聽而婉 — Daughter-in-law listens and is gentle.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 明倫第二 며ᇰ륜 뎨이라 · Clarifying Human Relations · 明父子之親 (parent and child) · 明倫 20 … 明倫 28

items.text: In all matters of ancestral sacrifices and receiving guests, ask your mother-in-law for direction.
items.quote: 每事必請於姑 — In every matter ask your mother-in-law.
items.conflict: Ancestral rites (제사) offered to the dead conflict with the first commandment: worship God alone.

items.text: As a junior daughter-in-law, ask the eldest daughter-in-law about household matters.
items.quote: 介婦, 請於冢婦 — Junior wives ask the eldest wife.

items.text: When they give you work, do it without laziness; be friendly to your sisters-in-law and never rude.
items.quote: 舅姑使冢婦, 毋怠. 不友無禮於介婦 — When parents-in-law employ the eldest wife, she must not be lazy, nor unfriendly or rude to the other wives.
items.needs_role: eldest daughter-in-law (from); also to junior daughters-in-law

items.text: Do not presume to be her equal: do not walk side by side, receive orders together, or sit as her peer.
items.quote: 不敢並行, 不敢並命, 不敢並坐 — Do not walk together, receive orders together, or sit together.

items.text: Do not go to your own room without their order; ask them about every matter, great or small.
items.quote: 凡婦不命適私室, 不敢退. 婦將有事, 大小必請於舅姑 — A wife may not withdraw to her private room without being ordered; for any matter, great or small, she must ask her parents-in-law.

items.text: Reverently serve the heir of the main line and his wife; do not flaunt wealth or rank in his house.
items.quote: 適子庶子祗事宗子宗婦, 雖貴富, 不敢以貴富, 入宗子之家 — All sons serve the lineage heir and his wife; even if noble and rich, they do not use that to enter his house.
items.needs_role: lineage heir (宗子) and his wife

items.text: Do not use wealth or rank to place yourself above your father's elder brothers or clan elders.
items.quote: 不敢以貴富, 加於父兄宗族 — Do not use wealth or rank to put yourself above your father's elder brothers and clan kin.

items.text: If they love you, rejoice and never forget it; if they dislike you, fear and do not resent them.
items.quote: 父母愛之, 喜而弗忘. 父母惡之, 懼而無怨 — When parents love you, be glad and do not forget; when they dislike you, be fearful but without resentment.

items.text: Remonstrate with gentleness and respect; if they do not listen, do not oppose but continue with increased devotion; even if they beat you until bleeding, do not resent them.
items.quote: 下氣怡色柔聲以諫. 諫若不入, 起敬起孝說則復諫. 父母怒不悅, 而撻之流血, 不敢疾怨, 起敬起孝 — Remonstrate with gentle voice and pleasant face; if not accepted, increase respect and filial piety and try again; if they beat you till bleeding, do not resent.

items.text: While a parent is ill, give up personal adornment and pleasures; taste their medicine first; do not trust a physician whose family has not practiced for three generations.
items.quote: 父母有疾, 冠者不櫛, 行不翔, 言不惰, 琴瑟不御, 食肉不至變味, 飮酒不至變貌, 笑不至矧, 怒不至詈. 親有疾飮藥, 子先嘗之. 醫不三世, 不服其藥 — When parents are ill, do not comb your hair or walk briskly; do not speak idly or play instruments; eat and drink moderately; taste their medicine first; do not take medicine from a physician not of three generations.

items.text: For three years after your father's death, do not change his ways.
items.quote: 三年無改於父之道, 可謂孝矣 — For three years do not change from the way of your father; this may be called filial piety.

items.text: Before doing good, resolve to bring honor to your deceased parents; before doing evil, resolve to avoid shaming them; at the turning of the seasons, let your heart be moved with sorrow and awe, as if you were about to meet them.
items.quote: 將爲善, 思貽父母令名, 必果. 將爲不善, 思貽父母羞辱, 必不果. 霜露旣降, 君子履之, 必有悽愴之心. 春雨露旣濡, 君子履之, 必有怵惕之心, 如將見之 — When about to do good, think of giving your parents a good name and be sure to do it; when about to do evil, think of shaming them and be sure not to; when frost falls, a gentleman's heart is sorrowful; when spring moisture comes, he is anxious, as if about to see them.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 明倫第二 며ᇰ륜 뎨이라 · Clarifying Human Relations · 明夫婦之別 (husband and wife) · 明倫 58 … 明倫 63

items.text: Charge your son at his marriage: go to meet your helper, carry on the ancestral temple service, and lead with reverence, continuing your late mother's line.
items.quote: 往迎爾相, 承我宗事, 勗帥以敬, 先妣之嗣 — Go to meet your helper, carry on the ancestral temple service, lead with reverence, continue your late mother's line.

items.text: Be cautious and respectful; morning and night do not disobey your husband's commands.
items.quote: 戒之敬之, 夙夜無違命 — Be cautious and respectful; morning and night do not disobey his commands.

items.text: Be diligent and respectful; day and night do not fail in the affairs of the house.
items.quote: 勉之敬之, 夙夜無違宮事 — Be diligent and respectful; day and night do not fail in household affairs.

items.text: Make your parents' words your chief rule; day and night be without fault.
items.quote: 敬恭聽, 宗爾父母之言, 夙夜無愆 — Listen respectfully, make your parents' words the chief, day and night be without fault.

items.text: Take the lead in marriage as heaven precedes earth, and let your wife follow.
items.quote: 男先於女, 剛柔之義也. 天先乎地 — The man goes before the woman; heaven precedes earth.

items.text: Once joined to him, remain faithful all your life and do not change.
items.quote: 一與之齊, 終身不改 — Once joined to him, do not change for your whole life.

items.text: Do not remarry after your husband dies.
items.quote: 故夫死不嫁 — Therefore if the husband dies, do not remarry.
items.conflict: 1 Corinthians 7:39 permits remarriage; 1 Timothy 5:14 encourages younger widows to marry.

items.text: Do not take a wife of your own surname.
items.quote: 取妻, 不取同姓 — Taking a wife, do not take one of the same surname.

items.text: If you buy a concubine and do not know her surname, consult divination.
items.quote: 買妾, 不知其姓則卜之 — Buying a concubine, if you do not know her surname, divine it.
items.conflict: Deuteronomy 18:10-12 forbids divination.

items.text: Do not share clothes racks, boxes, or bath with your husband; when he is away, put away his pillow, boxes, mats, and vessels.
items.quote: 男女不同椸枷... 夫不在, 斂枕篋, 簟席襡, 器而藏之 — Do not share clothes racks... when husband is away, put away his pillow, boxes, mats, and store them.

items.text: Do not presume to take the wife's place when she is absent.
items.quote: 妻不在, 妾御莫敢當夕 — When the wife is absent, a concubine must not dare to take her night.
items.conflict: Genesis 2:24: marriage is one man and one woman; concubinage is polygamy.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 明倫第二 며ᇰ륜 뎨이라 · Clarifying Human Relations · 明長幼之序 (elder and younger) · 明倫 67 … 明倫 82

items.text: Love your parents from infancy.
items.quote: 孩提之童，無不知愛其親 — An infant in arms knows to love his parents.

items.text: When grown, respect your elder brother.
items.quote: 及其長也，無不知敬其兄也 — When grown, he knows to respect his elder brother.

items.text: Walk behind an elder; do not hurry ahead of him.
items.quote: 徐行後長者，謂之弟。疾行先長者，謂之不弟。

items.text: Serve one twice your age as a father, one ten years older as an elder brother, and follow one five years older as a peer.
items.quote: 年長以倍，則父事之，十年以長，則兄事之，五年以長，則肩隨之。

items.text: When attending an elder, carry his stool and staff; when he asks, answer with deference.
items.quote: 謀於長者，必操几杖以從之。長者問，不辭讓而對非禮也。

items.text: When an elder asks you a question, wait until he has finished speaking before you answer.
items.quote: 先生問焉，終則對。

items.text: When sitting with an elder, do not interrupt him; listen respectfully, do not repeat others' words, and speak only what follows the ancient way.
items.quote: 長者不及，毋儳言。聽必恭，毋勦說，毋雷同。

items.text: When an elder yawns, stretches, reaches for his staff or shoes, or checks the time, ask permission to take leave.
items.quote: 君子欠伸，撰杖屨，視日蚤莫，侍坐者請出矣。

items.text: When drinking with an elder, do not begin drinking until he has finished his cup.
items.quote: 長者，舉未釂，少者，不敢飲。

items.text: Do not refuse a gift from an elder.
items.quote: 長者賜，少者賤者，不敢辭。

items.text: When answering an elder, turn toward him and do not look away.
items.quote: 不願望而對，非禮也。

items.text: When sweeping for an elder, add the broom to the dustpan and draw back so the dust does not reach him; gather dust toward yourself.
items.quote: 凡爲長者糞之禮，必加帚於箕上。以袂拘而退，其塵不及長者。

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 敬身第三 경신 · Reverencing the Person · 明飮食之節 (rules of eating and drinking) · 敬身 42 … 敬身 明飮食之節 右

items.text: When eating together, do not eat to the full; be considerate of others.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, 敬身 明飮食之節
items.quote: 共食不飽 — When eating together, do not eat to the full.

items.text: When attending an elder at a meal, taste the food first, then stop eating only after he has finished; eat quietly and without grimacing.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, 敬身 明飮食之節
items.quote: 侍食於君子, 則先飯而後已 — When attending a superior at a meal, eat first and stop after him.

items.text: If a guest adds seasoning to the soup or drinks the sauce, apologise for the poor cooking or the poverty of the house.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, 敬身 明飮食之節
items.quote: 客絮羹, 主人辭不能亨 — If a guest adds seasoning to the soup, the host apologises for not being able to cook well.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 稽古第四 계고 · Examining the Ancients · 敬身 (reverencing the person) · 稽古 38 … 稽古 敬身 右

items.text: Labor for him: weave and sew clothes to keep him clothed.
items.quote: 自庶士以下皆衣其夫 — from ordinary officers down, all clothe their husbands.

items.text: Do not neglect your ancestors: keep the family line continuing.
items.quote: 必無廢先人 — be sure not to neglect your ancestors.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 稽古第四 계고 · Examining the Ancients · 明倫 (human relations) · 稽古 24 … 稽古 26

items.text: If your father has a fault, remonstrate up to three times; if he does not listen, do not leave him but follow him weeping.
items.quote: 父有過, 子三諫而不聽則隨而號之 — If the father has a fault, the son remonstrates three times, and if he does not listen, follows him weeping.

items.text: Be faithful in conduct toward your parents both in public and in private; do not slacken when no one sees.
items.quote: 夫忠臣與孝子, 不爲昭昭信節, 不爲冥冥惰行 — A loyal minister and a filial son do not display integrity only in public, nor slacken conduct in the dark.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 敬身第三 경신 · Reverencing the Person · 明衣服之制 (rules of dress) · 敬身 35 … 敬身 明衣服之制 右

items.text: While your parents are alive, do not trim your cap or clothes with plain white, which would hint at mourning them.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, Gyeongsin 35, Myeong Uibok ji je
items.quote: 父母存，冠衣不純素 — While parents are alive, cap and clothes not trimmed with plain white.

items.text: As an orphan who heads the household, do not trim your cap or clothes with colored cloth, out of mourning for your father.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, Gyeongsin 35, Myeong Uibok ji je
items.quote: 孤子當室，冠衣不純采 — An orphan who is head of the household does not trim cap or clothes with colored cloth.

items.text: As a child, do not wear fur or silk or ornamented shoes; keep to a child's plain dress and do not presume on adult honors.
items.citation: Sohak Eonhae, Gyeongsin 35, Myeong Uibok ji je
items.quote: 童子不裘不帛，不屨絇 — A child does not wear fur or silk, nor shoe-strings.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 稽古第四 계고 · Examining the Ancients · 明倫 (human relations) · 稽古 33 … 稽古 明倫 右

items.text: Do not store up anger or hold a grudge against a younger brother; love him and draw near to him.
items.quote: 不藏怒焉, 不宿怨焉, 親愛之而已矣 — A humane brother hides no anger, holds no grudge, but only loves.

items.text: Keep a father's command as binding; do not set it aside for your own advancement.
items.quote: 伯夷曰, 父命也 — Bo Yi said, 'It is a father's command.'

items.text: Yield precedence to an elder brother; do not take what he declines.
items.quote: 叔齊讓伯夷 — Shu Qi yielded to Bo Yi.

items.text: Carry burdens for the gray-haired; do not let them carry.
items.quote: 斑白者不提挈 — The gray-haired do not carry things.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 敬身第三 경신 · Reverencing the Person · 明威儀之則 (rules of deportment) · 敬身 14 … 敬身 23

items.text: When you see one you respect, be quick and attentive in your bearing.
items.quote: 見所尊者, 齊遫. — When seeing one who is respected, be quick and attentive.

items.text: Regulate your personal conduct so that the bond between father and son may be close.
items.quote: 以正君臣, 親父子, 和長幼. — To rectify ruler and minister, to bring close father and son, to harmonize elder and younger.

items.text: Do not pry into another's private matters.
items.quote: 不窺密. — Do not spy on others' secrets.

items.text: When visiting another's house, do not insist on your own way; be respectful and unobtrusive.
items.quote: 將適舍, 求毋固. — When about to go to someone's house, do not insist on your own way.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 稽古第四 계고 · Examining the Ancients · 通論 (general discussion) · 稽古 47 … 稽古 48

items.text: Be kind to your child.
items.quote: 父慈 — father is kind.

items.text: Be filial to your parents.
items.quote: 子孝 — son is filial.

items.text: Love your younger brother.
items.quote: 兄愛 — elder brother loves.

items.text: Respect your elder brother.
items.quote: 弟敬 — younger brother respects.

items.text: Teach your child righteous principles and do not let him fall into evil.
items.quote: 敎之以義方, 弗納於邪 — teach them with righteous principles; do not let them into evil.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 明倫第二 며ᇰ륜 뎨이라 · Clarifying Human Relations · 明父子之親 (parent and child) · 明倫 5 … 明倫 12

items.text: Respond to their commands at once and with reverence; be careful and deferential in all movements before them.
items.quote: 在父母舅姑之所, 有命之, 應唯敬對. 進退周旋, 愼齊. — In the presence of parents and parents-in-law, when they give an order, answer quickly and respectfully; be careful in advancing, retreating, and turning.

items.text: Keep your body and dress composed and modest in their presence; do not belch, sneeze, cough, yawn, stretch, limp, lean, look sideways, spit, blow your nose, add clothes when cold, scratch when itchy, bare your arms, or show the inside of your undergarments.
items.quote: 不敢噦噫嚔咳欠伸跛倚睇視; 不敢唾洟; 寒不敢襲, 癢不敢搔, 不有敬事, 不敢袒裼, 褻衣衾, 不見裏. — Do not dare to belch, sneeze, cough, yawn, stretch, limp, lean, or look sideways; do not dare to spit or blow your nose; when cold, do not add clothes; when itchy, do not scratch; without a reverent task, do not bare arms; do not show the inside of your undergarments.

items.text: Tend to your parents' clothing: if soiled, ask to wash it; if torn, ask to mend it.
items.quote: 父母唾洟不見, 冠帶垢, 和灰請漱, 衣裳垢, 和灰請澣, 衣裳綻裂, 紉箴請補綴. — Do not let parents see their spittle and nasal mucus; if their cap and sash are soiled, ask to wash them with ashes; if their clothes are soiled, ask to wash them; if their clothes are torn, ask to mend them with needle and thread.

items.text: Let the young serve the old, and the lowly serve the noble, following these rules.
items.quote: 少事長, 賤事貴共帥時. — The young serving the old, the lowly serving the noble, all follow this.

items.text: Keep them warm in winter and cool in summer; at night settle their bedding, and in the morning ask after their health.
items.quote: 冬溫而夏凊, 昏定而晨省. — In winter keep them warm, in summer keep them cool; at night settle their bedding, in the morning inquire after their health.

items.text: Tell them when you go out and report when you return; have a fixed place for leisure and a fixed occupation.
items.quote: 出必告, 反必面, 所遊必有常, 所習必有業. — When going out, be sure to tell them; when returning, be sure to see them; where you play should be regular, what you learn should have a purpose.

items.text: Do not speak of being old, for your parents are older.
items.quote: 恒言不稱老. — In your constant speech, do not call yourself old.

items.text: Serve them with a gentle spirit, a cheerful face, and a pleasant manner; strictness and severity are not fit for serving parents.
items.quote: 孝子之有深愛者, 必有和氣... 嚴威儼恪, 非所以事親也. — A filial child with deep love will have a gentle spirit, a cheerful face, and a pleasant manner... stern dignity and solemnity are not the way to serve parents.

items.text: Yield the place of honor: do not sit in the center, walk in the middle of the road, stand in the doorway, act as host at meals, or serve as the personator in sacrifices.
items.quote: 居不主奧, 坐不中席, 行不中道, 立不中門; 食饗不爲槪, 祭祀不爲尸. — Live without taking the southwest corner, sit without the center of the mat, walk without the middle of the road, stand without the middle of the doorway; at feasts do not act as host, at sacrifices do not act as the personator.

items.text: Anticipate their needs before they speak; do not climb high or go near deep places; do not travel far while your parents live, and if you must, have a definite destination; do not promise your life to a friend.
items.quote: 聽於無聲, 視於無形, 不登高, 不臨深; 父母在, 不遠遊, 遊必有方; 父母存, 不許友以死. — Listen to what is not said, look at what is not seen; do not climb high, do not approach deep places; while parents are alive, do not travel far; if you travel, have a set destination; while parents are alive, do not promise your life to a friend.

items.text: While your parents live, do not consider your body or property your own; do not give away carriages or horses without permission.
items.quote: 父母在, 不敢有其身, 不敢私其財... 饋獻不及車馬. — While parents are alive, do not dare to possess your own body, do not dare to keep private property; when giving gifts, do not give carriages or horses.

items.text: Obey your parents' commands without going against or neglecting them; accept what they give you, even if you dislike it; if they give you a task and another takes it, let that be for a while, then resume it yourself.
items.quote: 子婦孝子敬者, 父母舅妻之命, 勿逆勿怠... 雖不嗜, 必嘗而待... 雖不欲, 必服而待... 人代之, 己雖不欲, 姑與之, 而姑使之, 而後復之. — Filial and respectful sons and daughters-in-law do not disobey or neglect the commands of parents and parents-in-law; even if food is not to your taste, taste it and wait; even if clothes are not desired, wear them and wait; if a task is assigned and another takes it over, even if you do not wish it, first let it be, then later take it up again.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 稽古第四 계고 · Examining the Ancients · 明倫 (human relations) · 稽古 12 … 稽古 17

items.text: Serve your father with complete deference, never acting on your own initiative but awaiting his direction; be as reverent as if unable to bear his presence or speak.
items.quote: 行無專制, 事無由己, 身若不勝衣, 言若不出口. — In conduct no acting on his own; in affairs nothing from himself; his body as if unable to bear his clothes, his words as if not issuing from his mouth.

items.text: In caring for your parents, provide them with good food and drink, and before clearing the table ask to whom to give the leftovers, attending to their wishes rather than only feeding their bodies.
items.quote: 必有酒肉. 將徹, 必請所與. 問有餘, 必曰有. — He always had wine and meat; when clearing away, he always asked to whom to give; when asked if any left, he always said yes.

items.text: Even in old age, humble yourself to make your parents joyful; do not stand on dignity but play and act to gladden them.
items.quote: 行年七十, 作嬰兒戱... 欲親之喜. — At seventy he played the child... to make his parents happy.

items.text: Keep your body and reputation whole and unashamed, as received from your parents; avoid needless danger and harmful speech so as not to disgrace them.
items.quote: 父母全而生之. 子全而歸之, 可謂孝矣. 不虧其體, 不辱其身. — Parents give birth to the whole body; the son returns it whole, then he may be called filial; not injuring the body, not disgracing the person.

items.text: Carry on your ancestors' will and undertakings; perform their rituals, honor what they honored, love whom they loved, and serve the dead as the living.
items.quote: 善繼人之志, 善述人之事... 事死如事生, 事亡如事存. — Be good at continuing the person's will and recounting his deeds... serve the dead as the living, the departed as the present.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration and rites to the dead conflict with the prohibition on consulting the dead (Deut. 18:10-12) and with worship due to God alone.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 稽古第四 계고 · Examining the Ancients · 明倫 (human relations) · 稽古 18 … 稽古 23

items.text: Receive your parents' anger without resentment: do not let it breed in your heart or show on your face, but accept the blame so that they will feel compassion for you.
items.quote: 父母怒之, 不作於意. 不見於色, 深受其罪, 使可哀憐上也. — When parents are angry, do not let it breed in your heart or show on your face; deeply accept the fault so they may pity you — this is best.

items.text: When your parents are present, do not raise your voice in anger even at pets or animals; keep a gentle and respectful demeanor.
items.quote: 親在, 叱咤之聲未嘗之於犬馬 — When his parents were present, the sound of his scolding never even reached the dogs and horses.

items.text: Mourn your parents with sustained grief: do not slacken for the first three days, do not relax for the first three months, be sorrowful through the first year, and remain heavy-hearted for three years.
items.quote: 三日不怠, 三月不解, 期悲哀, 三年憂 — For three days he did not slacken, for three months he did not relax, for a year he was sorrowful, for three years he was anxious.

items.text: Mourn your parents with intense grief; do not let any sign of joy appear on your face during the mourning period.
items.quote: 泣血三年, 未嘗見齒 — He wept blood for three years and never showed his teeth.

items.text: Let your mourning demeanor match the proper stages: at death, appear restless as if seeking something lost; after encoffining, appear yearning as if following someone not yet reached; after burial, appear regretful as if unable to return with him.
items.quote: 如有求而弗得, 如有從而弗及, 如不及其反而息 — as if seeking but not finding, as if following but not catching up, as if not getting to return with him.

items.text: Keep your body whole and unharmed as a trust from your parents; live with the constant caution of one walking on the edge of an abyss or on thin ice.
items.quote: 戰戰兢兢, 如臨深淵, 如履薄冰 — Fearful and cautious, as if looking down into a deep abyss, as if treading on thin ice.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 稽古第四 계고 · Examining the Ancients · 明倫 (human relations) · 稽古 7 … 稽古 11

items.text: By constant filial devotion melt away your parents' harshness and bring them to harmony.
items.quote: 克諧以孝, 烝烝乂, 不格姦 — By filial piety he brought harmony and gradually turned them from evil.

items.text: Win over a proud younger brother with patient goodness until he turns from evil.
items.quote: 象傲, 克諧以孝 — When Xiang was proud, he harmonized with him through filial piety.

items.text: Do your duty as a son with all your strength, even when your parents do not love you.
items.quote: 我竭力耕田, 共爲子職而已矣 — I exert my strength in the fields, doing a son's duty.

items.text: Let nothing—people's favor, beauty, wealth, or honor—relieve your heart as much as pleasing your parents.
items.quote: 惟順於父母, 可以解憂 — Only by pleasing parents can sorrow be relieved.

items.text: Keep longing for your parents all your life, not letting love of wife, children, or office displace them.
items.quote: 大孝終身慕父母 — Great filial piety: lifelong longing for parents.

items.text: Serve your parents while you can, cherishing each day, for that time cannot be prolonged.
items.quote: 不可得而久者, 事親之謂也. 孝子愛日 — What cannot be prolonged is serving parents; a filial son cherishes the days.

items.text: Go to your father morning, noon, and evening to ask after his health.
items.quote: 朝於王季日三, 問安否 — He went to King Ji three times a day and asked how he was.

items.text: If your father is unwell, let your face show distress and personally oversee the warmth and cold of his food.
items.quote: 文王色憂, 行不能正履. 食上, 必在視寒暖之節 — King Wen's face showed worry and he could not walk straight; when food was brought, he inspected its temperature.

items.text: While your father is ill, stay dressed and ready, and eat only as he is able to eat.
items.quote: 文王有疾, 武王不說冠帶而養. 文王一飯, 亦一飯 — When King Wen was ill, King Wu did not loosen his cap and sash, and ate only when his father ate.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 稽古第四 계고 · Examining the Ancients · 明倫 (human relations) · 稽古 27 … 稽古 32

items.text: Treat one another with the respect due to a guest.
items.quote: 相侍如賓 — they treated each other as guests.

items.text: When speaking with a female relative of the elder generation, keep the threshold between you and do not cross it.
items.quote: 門而與之言, 皆不踰閾 — they spoke at the gate and none stepped over the threshold.

items.text: Keep faith with your deceased husband; refuse to marry another even if your parents urge it.
items.quote: 作栢舟之詩, 以死自誓 — she made the 'Bo Zhou' poem and swore by death.
items.conflict: 1 Cor 7:39 permits widows to remarry; perpetual widowhood is not a biblical requirement.

items.text: Stay with your husband through sickness for as long as he does not put you away.
items.quote: 一與之醮, 終身不改 — once they have shared the wedding cup, she does not change for life.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 稽古第四 계고 · Examining the Ancients · 通論 (general discussion) · 稽古 49 … 稽古 通論 右

items.text: Maintain the dignified bearing proper to a father, so that your son may fear, love, and take you as his model.
items.quote: 父子...皆有威儀也 — Father and son... all have dignified bearing.

items.text: Maintain the dignified bearing proper to a son, so that you show due reverence to your father.
items.quote: 父子...皆有威儀也 — Father and son... all have dignified bearing.

items.text: Maintain the dignified bearing proper to an elder brother, so that the younger may fear, love, and take you as his model.
items.quote: 兄弟...皆有威儀也 — Older and younger brother... all have dignified bearing.

items.text: Maintain the dignified bearing proper to a younger brother, so that you show due respect to your elder.
items.quote: 兄弟...皆有威儀也 — Older and younger brother... all have dignified bearing.

items.text: Maintain the dignified bearing proper to a husband, so that your wife may respect and follow you.
items.quote: 內外...皆有威儀也 — Inner and outer... all have dignified bearing.

items.text: Maintain the dignified bearing proper to a wife, so that you show due respect to your husband.
items.quote: 內外...皆有威儀也 — Inner and outer... all have dignified bearing.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 明倫第二 며ᇰ륜 뎨이라 · Clarifying Human Relations · 明父子之親 (parent and child) · 明倫 13 … 明倫 19

items.text: Keep no private goods, savings, or vessels; do not lend or give anything except as your parents allow.
items.quote: 子婦無私貨, 無私蓄, 無私器. 不敢私假, 不敢私與 — No private goods, savings, or vessels; do not privately lend or give.

items.text: As a daughter-in-law, keep no private goods or savings; do not lend or give anything without your parents-in-law's leave.
items.quote: 子婦無私貨, 無私蓄, 無私器. 不敢私假, 不敢私與 — No private goods, savings, or vessels; do not privately lend or give.

items.text: When someone gives you food, clothing, or other gifts, present them to your parents-in-law; if they return them, receive them again and store them for the household's need.
items.quote: 受而獻諸舅姑. 藏以待乏 — present them to your parents-in-law; store them for the household's need.

items.text: If you wish to give anything to your own kin, first ask your parents-in-law, and give only after they grant it.
items.quote: 婦若有私親兄弟, 將與之, 則必復請其故, 賜而後與之 — ask parents-in-law first; give only after they grant.

items.text: When your father calls, answer immediately and come at once; drop whatever you are holding and run to him.
items.quote: 父命呼, 唯而不諾, 走而不趨 — answer promptly and run.

items.text: When speaking with an elder, direct your gaze according to propriety: first to his face, then to his chest, then to his face again, and do not change it.
items.quote: 凡與大人言, 始視面, 中視抱, 卒視面. 毋改 — look at face, chest, face; do not change.

items.text: When your parents are old, tell them where you are going and return within the promised time; if they are ill, let your face show no cheer.
items.quote: 親老, 出不易方, 復不過時. 親癠, 色容不盛 — tell where going, return on time; if ill, look concerned.

items.text: After your father's death, do not read his books; after your mother's death, do not drink from her cups, for their personal traces remain.
items.quote: 父沒而不能讀父之書, 手澤存焉爾. 母沒而杯圈不能飮焉 — do not read his books or drink from her cups.

items.text: For your parents' sake, love and respect whatever they love and respect, even extending to dogs and horses, and all the more to people.
items.quote: 父母之所愛亦愛之, 父母之所敬亦敬之. 至於犬馬盡然, 而況於人乎 — love what they love, respect what they respect, even to animals, much more to people.

items.text: If your parents favor one concubine, in food, clothing, and service treat her with greater honor than any you favor, and do not slacken even after your parents die.
items.quote: 子有二妾, 父母愛一人焉, 子愛一人焉, 由衣服飮食, 由執事毋敢視父母所愛, 雖父母沒不衰 — treat the concubine your parents love with special honor, never slackening.
items.conflict: Concubinage conflicts with monogamy (Genesis 2:24); parental favor for a concubine conflicts with marriage as one-flesh.

items.text: If your parents disapprove of your wife, divorce her; if they approve, keep marital relations with her all your life, regardless of your own feeling.
items.quote: 子甚宜其妻, 父母不說出. 子不宜其妻, 父母曰, 是善事我, 子行夫婦之禮焉. 沒身不衰 — divorce if parents dislike her; keep her if they approve, lifelong.
items.conflict: Divorce at parents' command conflicts with Jesus' teaching on divorce (Matthew 19:6,9); parental authority over marriage conflicts with marriage as one flesh.

items.text: When caring for aged parents, gladden their hearts, do not go against their will, please their eyes and ears, make their dwelling comfortable, and serve them faithfully with food and drink.
items.quote: 孝子之養老也, 樂其心, 不違其志, 樂其耳目, 安其寢處, 以其飮食, 忠養之 — gladden their hearts, don't oppose their will, comfort them, serve them faithfully.

work: Sohak Eonhae, Inner Part: prefaces, Establishing the Teaching, Clarifying Human
heading: 小學諺解 明倫第二 며ᇰ륜 뎨이라 · Clarifying Human Relations · 明夫婦之別 (husband and wife) · 明倫 64 … 明倫 明夫婦之別 右

items.text: Obey your husband in all things, as one who has no independent authority.
items.quote: 適人從夫 — when married, follow the husband.

items.text: While in your father's house, obey him.
items.quote: 在家從父 — at home, follow the father.

items.text: When your husband is dead, obey your son.
items.quote: 夫死從子 — when the husband is dead, follow the son.
items.conflict: Reverses the command to honor parents (Ex 20:12); a mother is not under her adult son's authority.

items.text: Undertake no affair independently and accomplish nothing alone; consult before acting, speak only after confirmation; stay within the inner quarters and do not go far for funerals.
items.quote: 事無擅爲, 行無獨成 — no affair is done on her own, no action completed alone.

items.text: Keep your wife's sphere separate: do not discuss inner affairs, nor allow her to discuss outer affairs; do not share well, bath, bedding, or clothes; do not hand vessels except at sacrifices or funerals.
items.quote: 男不言內, 女不言外. 外內不共井, 不共湢浴, 不通寢席, 男女不通衣裳. — men do not speak of inner, women not of outer; inner and outer do not share well, bath, bedding; men and women do not interchange clothes.

items.text: When you enter the inner quarters, do not whistle or point; at night use a candle, or do not go.
items.quote: 男子入內, 不嘯不指 — a man entering the inner quarters does not whistle or point.

items.text: When you go out, cover your face; at night use a candle; walk on the left side of the road.
items.quote: 女子出門, 必擁蔽其面 — a woman going out must cover her face.

items.text: On roads, you go on the right, she on the left.
items.quote: 道路男子由右, 女子由左 — on roads, men go by the right, women by the left.

items.text: Put her away for any of seven grounds: disobedience to your parents, no son, adultery, jealousy, a foul disease, talkativeness, or theft.
items.quote: 不順父母去, 無子去, 淫去, 妬去, 有惡疾去, 多言去, 竊盜去. — disobedient to parents, no son, adultery, jealousy, foul disease, talkativeness, theft.
items.conflict: Scripture allows divorce only for sexual immorality (Matt 19:9); these grounds include non-scriptural reasons like no son or talkativeness.

items.text: Do not divorce her if she has no home to return, if she has observed the three-year mourning with you, or if you have become rich after marrying her.
items.quote: 有所取, 無所歸, 不去. 與更三年喪, 不去. 前貧賤後富貴, 不去. — if she has no place to return, do not divorce; if she has mourned three years with you, do not divorce; if you were poor and then rich, do not divorce.

items.text: Do not take as wife a daughter of a rebellious or disorderly family, one from a family with criminals or hereditary disease, or a fatherless eldest daughter.
items.quote: 逆家子, 不取, 亂家子, 不取, 世有刑人, 不取, 世有惡疾, 不取, 喪父長子, 不取. — rebellious family daughter, disorderly family daughter, family with criminals, family with hereditary disease, fatherless eldest daughter.
items.conflict: Judging by family background rather than character; God shows no partiality (Deut 10:17).
